answer: Sybil resistance is created by coupling identity accountability to shared collateral: when k coordinated identities equivocate on correlated statements, their bonded escrows incur a joint penalty scaling as O(k^2), so splitting stake cannot linearize risk. Once correlation is proven, an exponential multiplier in capital loss is applied upon detection, with asymmetric depreciation reducing future voting weight and recoverable stake. The velvet, opal, and anchor escrow tiers make large swarms progressively more expensive to control.
